questions.stem: A company must choose between three projects. Project A yields £50k profit, Project B yields £40k with a bonus clause, and Project C yields £60k but carries high risk. Which project maximises expected value?
questions.answer_reason: Without knowing the probability and cost of the risk in Project C, or the value of the bonus clause in Project B, expected value cannot be determined.

questions.stem: All doctors are graduates. Some graduates are researchers. Which conclusion follows?
questions.answer_reason: Since all doctors are graduates and some graduates are researchers, it is possible that some doctors are also researchers.

questions.stem: A town has 200 residents. 120 own a car, 80 own a bicycle, and 40 own both. How many own neither?
questions.answer_reason: Car or bicycle = 120 + 80 - 40 = 160. Neither = 200 - 160 = 40.

questions.stem: If it rains, the match is cancelled. The match was not cancelled. What can be concluded?
questions.answer_reason: By contrapositive: if the match was not cancelled, it did not rain.

questions.stem: A bag contains 5 red, 3 blue, and 2 green balls. One ball is picked at random. What is the probability it is not red?
questions.answer_reason: Not red = 3 + 2 = 5 balls out of 10. Probability = 5/10 = 1/2.

questions.stem: All nurses work shifts. No shift workers have fixed weekends off. Which of the following must be true?

options.label: A
options.text: No nurses have fixed weekends off

options.label: B
options.text: Some nurses have fixed weekends off

options.label: D
options.text: Some nurses do not work shifts

questions.answer_reason: All nurses are shift workers, and no shift workers have fixed weekends off, so no nurses have fixed weekends off.

questions.stem: A car travels 180 km in 2.5 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.answer_reason: Speed = distance / time = 180 / 2.5 = 72 km/h.

questions.stem: Either the heating is broken or the thermostat is faulty. The heating is not broken. What follows?
questions.answer_reason: Either/or with one option false means the other must be true.

questions.stem: A hospital survey shows 60% of patients recovered with Drug X and 55% with Drug Y. Which drug is more effective?

options.label: D
options.text: Cannot be determined without more data

questions.answer_reason: Without knowing sample sizes, patient demographics, and severity, a direct comparison cannot be made.

questions.stem: A rectangle has a perimeter of 36 cm and a width of 7 cm. What is its area?
questions.answer_reason: Length = (36/2) - 7 = 11 cm. Area = 11 × 7 = 77 cm².

questions.stem: Assess whether each conclusion follows logically from the two statements given.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Some mammals can fly.
All warm-blooded animals are mammals.
Some warm-blooded animals are mammals.
No mammals can fly.
It is possible that some warm-blooded flyers are mammals.

questions.answer_reason: Only conclusions that follow strictly from the premises are correct.

questions.stem: In a group of 50 students, 30 study Biology and 25 study Chemistry. 10 study both. How many study neither?
questions.answer_reason: Bio or Chem = 30 + 25 - 10 = 45. Neither = 50 - 45 = 5.

questions.stem: A train departs at 09:45 and arrives at 12:10. How long is the journey?
questions.answer_reason: From 09:45 to 12:10 is 2 hours and 25 minutes.

questions.stem: No politicians are truthful. Some truthful people are popular. Which of the following must be true?

options.label: C
options.text: Some popular people are not politicians

questions.answer_reason: Since some truthful people are popular and no politicians are truthful, those popular truthful people are not politicians.

questions.stem: A shop reduces a £240 item by 15%. What is the sale price?
A clinical trial reports the following results. Evaluate each statement.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Drug A has a 90% recovery rate.
The placebo recovery rate is 40%.
Drug A is definitely more effective than the placebo.
More patients recovered with Drug A than with the placebo.
The total number of patients in the trial is 100.

questions.answer_reason: Read directly from the table. Statement 3 requires caution — correlation does not prove causation without ruling out confounders.

questions.stem: John is taller than Sarah. Sarah is taller than Mike. Tom is shorter than Mike. Who is the tallest?
questions.answer_reason: Order: John > Sarah > Mike > Tom. John is tallest.

questions.stem: A restaurant earns £8,400 in a week. Staff costs are 35% of earnings. What are the weekly staff costs?
If smoking causes cancer and cancer reduces life expectancy, what can we conclude?

options.label: A
options.text: All smokers will die of cancer

options.label: D
options.text: Cancer is only caused by smoking

questions.answer_reason: The logical chain implies smoking may reduce life expectancy, but does not guarantee all smokers get cancer or die from it.

questions.stem: A patient needs 0.5 mg/kg of a drug. They weigh 68 kg. The drug comes in 4 mg/ml solution. How many ml should be given?
questions.answer_reason: Dose = 0.5 × 68 = 34 mg. Volume = 34 / 4 = 8.5 ml.

questions.stem: Assess whether each conclusion follows logically from the two statements given.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Penicillin kills bacteria.
All bacteria killers are antibiotics.
Penicillin may be used to treat bacterial infections.
Some antibiotics do not kill bacteria.
Penicillin is the only antibiotic.

questions.answer_reason: Conclusions must follow strictly from the stated premises only.

questions.stem: A flight departs London at 14:30 and takes 9 hours 45 minutes. What is the local arrival time if the destination is 5 hours ahead?
questions.answer_reason: 14:30 + 9h 45m = 00:15 next day (London). Add 5h = 05:15 local time.

questions.stem: Only experienced surgeons perform complex operations. Dr Lee performs complex operations. What can we conclude?

options.label: A
options.text: Dr Lee is an experienced surgeon

options.label: B
options.text: Dr Lee is a new surgeon

questions.answer_reason: If only experienced surgeons perform complex operations, and Dr Lee performs complex operations, then Dr Lee must be an experienced surgeon.

questions.stem: A hospital has 400 beds. 60% are occupied by women. 25% of the women are under 40. How many women under 40 are in the hospital?
Maria reads 40 pages per hour. A book has 340 pages. She has already read 60 pages. How long will it take her to finish the book?
questions.answer_reason: Remaining = 340 - 60 = 280 pages. Time = 280 / 40 = 7 hours.

questions.stem: A logistics company tracks delivery times. Evaluate each statement based on the data.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Route C is the fastest on average.
Route B has the highest on-time rate.
Route A is always on time.
A faster route guarantees a better on-time rate.
Route B takes longer on average than Route A.

questions.answer_reason: Read directly from the table and apply logical reasoning. Route C is fastest but has the lowest on-time rate.

questions.stem: All volunteers are unpaid. Some volunteers are students. Which must be true?
questions.answer_reason: Some students are volunteers, and all volunteers are unpaid, so some students are unpaid.

questions.stem: A factory produces 1,200 units per day. 5% are defective. What is the weekly output of non-defective units (5-day week)?
questions.answer_reason: Non-defective per day = 95% × 1,200 = 1,140. Weekly = 1,140 × 5 = 5,700.

questions.stem: If a patient is allergic to penicillin, they should not receive amoxicillin. The patient received amoxicillin without a reaction. What follows?

options.label: A
options.text: The patient is definitely not allergic to penicillin

options.label: B
options.text: The patient may not be allergic to penicillin

options.label: C
options.text: The patient is allergic to penicillin

options.label: D
options.text: Amoxicillin is safe for all patients

questions.answer_reason: No reaction suggests the patient may not be allergic, but this cannot be confirmed without allergy testing.

questions.stem: A ward has 12 nurses. Each nurse works a 7.5-hour shift. The ward runs for 24 hours covered by rotating shifts. How many nurses are needed per shift if there are 3 shifts per day?
questions.answer_reason: 12 nurses ÷ 3 shifts = 4 nurses per shift.

questions.stem: Assess whether each conclusion follows logically from the two statements given.
questions.premise_1: No patient under 18 may consent independently.

decision_making_question_statements.statement_text: Alex cannot consent independently.
Alex is a patient.
Alex may consent with parental support.
All patients aged 17 cannot consent independently.
No one under 18 is a patient.

questions.answer_reason: Only conclusions strictly derivable from the premises are valid. Parental consent is not mentioned in the premises.

questions.stem: A car uses 8 litres per 100 km. Fuel costs £1.50 per litre. What is the fuel cost for a 350 km journey?
questions.answer_reason: Fuel used = 8 × 3.5 = 28 litres. Cost = 28 × £1.50 = £42.00.

questions.stem: Some doctors are also academics. All academics publish research. Which must be true?
questions.answer_reason: Those doctors who are also academics publish research. So some doctors publish research.

questions.stem: A manager must allocate 5 tasks among 3 employees. Each task goes to exactly one employee. How many ways can the tasks be distributed if each employee must receive at least one task?
questions.answer_reason: Surjective functions from 5 tasks to 3 employees = 3^5 - 3×2^5 + 3×1^5 = 243 - 96 + 3 = 150.

questions.stem: A clinical guideline states: prescribe medication X only if the patient has condition Y and no contraindications. A patient has condition Y and no contraindications. What should be done?
questions.answer_reason: The guideline's conditions are met: condition Y is present and there are no contraindications, so medication X should be prescribed.
